2611.33700.image_caption: Figure 1: Progressive degradation of a static sports agent. The upper panels illustrate query shifts, data drift, and model-capability misalignment; the lower panel shows declining weekly factual accuracy.

2611.33739.image_caption: Figure 1: RegHarness execution comparison and paired-trial success.

2611.33808.image_caption: Figure 1 : Motivation for EvoVAU. (a) Paradigm comparison. Existing VAU agents [ 46 , 41 , 31 , 26 ] adapt analysis within predefined workflow or harness, whereas EvoVAU evolves tools for a frozen solver using task feedback and an external proposer. (b) Improvement on the Development Set. Initial tools and EvoVAU use the same frozen solver. Subsets are defined by whether the solver invokes updated tools.

2611.33836.image_caption: Figure 1 : One round of LANTERN , shown on round 3. (1) The failure census assigns every missed validation lesion one cause. (2) The mentor pre-registers a hypothesis and implements one revision at one of four levels. (3) A frozen examiner accepts or rejects it on validation only ( Sec. 3 ).

2611.33879.image_caption: Figure 1: Overview of FORK. Left (deployment): the guardrail gates each tool call and reply; its public message after a rejection reaches the agent and the attacker, who adapts through user turns and tool observations. Right (co-evolution): each round selects opponents by maximin, runs informed interactions, verifies and reflects on outcomes, and updates the skill libraries.

2611.33909.image_caption: Figure 1 : Illustration of conditional skills distilled from historical agent dialogues for medical image interpretation. A conditional skill abstracts reusable reasoning patterns into three stages: identifying relevant cues, examining discriminative imaging features, and evaluating competing explanations. Without the skill, the ReAct agent blindly invokes tools, pursues misleading intermediate findings, and overlooks question-specific clinical cues, resulting in an incorrect diagnosis of pericardial cyst after nine tool calls and one execution failure. With the skill, the agent integrates imaging findings with anatomical context and correctly identifies a Morgagni hernia in only five tool calls.

2611.33915.image_caption: Figure 1 : Motivation and central idea of SEEK. Top: GPT-6 Astra [ 29 ] acting directly keeps what the robot learns only in its working context and loses it once the task ends, so the next attempt may repeat the same mistakes; on a real robot, the last cube of a square is again grasped and set down, leaving a gap. Bottom: SEEK retains this execution knowledge across attempts as action-effect evidence (PAEB), including that of failed attempts, and reusable procedures (SEPP), while the model remains fixed; its next attempt pushes the cube in. Right: with GPT-6.2 Astra on 34 RoboDojo tasks, task score by category and model requests per episode of SEEK after 5 attempts and of the model acting directly [ 38 ] .

2611.34250.image_caption: Figure 2: Skill-use accuracy (%) of nine models under two harnesses and four conditions. Models are ordered by increasing EBU gap averaged over the two harnesses; Δ below each group of bars is the EBU gap (pp). Error bars are Wilson 95% intervals (n = 154). †: task screening used GLM-5.1 from the same model family.

2611.34416.image_caption: Figure 1: A retrieval example of task-directed curiosity. A visibility-only robot acts on current observations. A curious robot proposes locations, seeks evidence, identifies missing capabilities, and acquires validated skills to enable retrieval. The right branch illustrates acquisition mode.

2611.34440.image_caption: Figure 1 : Overview of our proposed vSFT. Given a task, the hypernetwork first internalizes the system prompt and few-shot examples into an initial LoRA adapter, and then progressively incorporates the supervisor’s feedback through subsequent trial-and-error iterations, thereby adapting the agent over time.

2611.34624.image_caption: Figure 1: Overview of HoMe. The Developer Agents diagnose failures and edit the harness to generate candidates. The Experiment Manager records candidates and results, controls tool access, and plans evaluations. The Evaluation Environment evaluates candidates in isolated sandboxes.

2611.34675.image_caption: Figure 2 : P2H and H2P evolution. (a) P2H: for each failure in ℱ r \mathcal{F}_{r} , the VLM coding agent retrieves memory, diagnoses the failure, and searches Code, Code+ICL, and Code+Policy routes in parallel; it keeps the verified solution with the lowest jerk J ⁡ ( τ ) J(\tau) and merges compatible changes into the skills L L , memory M M , and routing ρ \rho of H ~ r + 1 \widetilde{H}_{r+1} . (b) H2P: verified trajectories and same-state success/failure pairs update the policy with SFT, CPD, and EWC under failure-aware task sampling; the updated policy starts round r + 1 r{+}1 .

2611.34760.image_caption: Figure 2: Overview of SEPO’s behavioral diversity evolution. In the inner loop (left), candidates are clustered in instruction space, the most behaviorally promising representative of each cluster seeds LLM-based evolution, and rollout evaluation filters the resulting candidates by quality. After m m evolution steps, the outer loop (right) scores all feasible candidates by their minimum divergence from the reference-augmented set 𝒜 k = { I 0 } ∪ 𝒮 k \mathcal{A}_{k}=\{I_{0}\}\cup\mathcal{S}_{k} and admits the farthest candidate into 𝒮 k + 1 \mathcal{S}_{k+1} . The diagram instantiates D ^ \widehat{D} with its token-level Jensen–Shannon (JS) surrogate, using the k 2 k_{2} estimator for KL. The default instruction I 0 I_{0} serves only as a novelty anchor and is excluded from the final mixture; all unselected candidates remain in the persistent pool for the next round.

2611.33183.image_caption: Figure 1: REI learns reusable ideation policies from repository evolution, while SPOD prevents semantic collapse by debiasing method families and retaining strong representatives.

2611.33195.image_caption: Figure 1: MatRecall converts verified prediction events into retrievable experience. a , LLM-only performs stateless prediction: each query is handled independently, without external memory or retained experience. b , Static RAG retrieves training input–output records from a fixed domain library, but completed predictions do not change that library. c , MatRecall retrieves both static evidence and verified episodes. The current outcome is revealed only after prediction; its task-native score triggers encoding of a new episode. d , The four-stage memory cycle predicts with static evidence, reveals and scores the outcome, encodes the completed execution, and reinstates relevant experience for later queries. Each episode binds the query q t q_{t} , actions a t a_{t} , retrieved evidence z t z_{t} , prediction y ^ t \hat{y}_{t} , verified outcome y t y_{t} , task-native metric ℓ t \ell_{t} , and compressed lesson m t m_{t} . The return arrow denotes that only previously scored episodes can inform a subsequent query.

2611.33612.image_caption: Figure 2: Memory operations in user 4’s own memory and adapted user 1 memory.

2611.33822.image_caption: Figure 3: MetaDecomp jointly learns a state space specified by schema Σ \Sigma and transition DAGs in that space. Retained state nodes and transition DAGs form the procedural memory ℋ \mathcal{H} . The inner loop refines a cached decomposition D base D^{\mathrm{base}} into D 0 D_{0} and revises it using actor feedback. Successful training executions update the shared knowledge between episodes; evaluation keeps it fixed. The illustrative binary fields denote established (1) or unestablished (0) progress.

2611.34762.image_caption: Figure 1 : Memory hallucination: the memory is correct, the answer is not. (a) Text-only memory or RAG puts the retrieved note into the prompt and leaves the rest to the frozen model, where the note in the context conflicts with the stale fact in the weights. On a question about the memory, the weights win and the model answers with the stale fact (Type I, memory-ignoring). On a question about another entity, the note wins and the model assigns the memory to the wrong entity (Type II, memory-misapplying). Across our five models these rates reach 46% and 24%, and Type II reaches 49% when retrieval is combined with weight editing. (b) TASK memory goes beyond text-only memory. Each memory object holds T ext content, a K nowledge edit Δ ​ W m \Delta W_{m} whose key u ^ m \hat{u}_{m} serves as the in-model address, and a pair of A ctivation- S teering vectors ( v + , v − ) (v^{+},v^{-}) that carry no content. For a query x x , the address response r m ​ ( x ) r_{m}(x) is compared with the threshold τ m \tau_{m} . A relevant query shows T , loads E and adds v + v^{+} , so the model adopts the memory; an unrelated query leaves T and E off and adds v − v^{-} , so the model keeps its own answer.

2611.33794.image_caption: Figure 2 : Who decides what the loop keeps. (a) The loop’s own judge. (b) An off-the-shelf judge: fooled less, still blind to unseen data. (c) SealedLoop : the improver trains with J in J_{\mathrm{in}} only, a sequential test on the sealed J out J_{\mathrm{out}} decides, and both judges score each generation.

2611.34303.image_caption: Figure 1: Overview of the methodology and evaluation pipeline.

2611.34398.image_caption: Figure 1: Task proficiency does not specify a compositional interface. (a) Skills that work alone and over two calls fail in one call. (b) Layout alone can suppress A A , and on two Qwen bases layout-augmented skills keep A A after a norm-matched block but not after trained B B . (c) A skill retrained next to frozen B B fails with B ′ B^{\prime} , a proficient block of the same operation (post hoc, medians on 0.5B and 1.5B). (d) Both edits raise one-call accuracy, but only the anchored edit, with twice the examples, keeps the edited skill.

2611.34400.image_caption: Figure 1: Overview of EvoLink-Bench factual and capability evolution in interdependent streams.

2611.34598.image_caption: Figure 1 : Comparison of hallucination evaluation workflows. (a) Existing evaluation pipelines construct test queries manually or with LLM assistance, using fixed test items or generation strategies without target-model feedback to guide further refinement. (b) SEAM (Ours) combines feedback-driven adaptive probing in an inner loop with skill evolution in an outer loop to uncover latent hallucination vulnerabilities. In the illustrated case, the queries ask about the color of a tennis player’s shoes. The target model correctly identifies the shoes as black in Question 1 and rejects the claim that they are white in Question 2, exhibiting no hallucination in either case. SEAM automatically generates Question 3 by introducing the misleading premise, inducing the model to incorrectly identify the shoes as white, which exposes the model’s enduring vulnerability to such hallucination risks.

2611.34612.image_caption: Figure 2: Empirical capability boundaries of FWSP. (a) Normalized Recovery Ratio ( NRR = ( After − Base ) / ( Oracle − Base ) \text{NRR}=(\text{After}-\text{Base})/(\text{Oracle}-\text{Base}) ) across regimes R1–R5. (b) Boundary summary across five modalities and six model families (50K to 8.2B parameters).

2611.34915.image_caption: Fig. 1: Memory is not ground truth. A previously verified object can fail current VLM verification either because the environment has changed or because perception has failed. An episode-local policy forgets earlier failed verification and can repeatedly revisit the same remembered location. Our method instead revises the memory’s navigation authority without asserting that the object is absent, redirects search toward a semantically selected frontier, and preserves the memory for future positive evidence. The inset in (c) shows frontier candidates in the deployed 2-D navigation representation.
